title: Spark's custody quorum requires signers from at least two independent entities, not merely three signatures
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.7.2.7.3 and A.6.1.1.1.3.8.2.7.3 state the rule identically: "Accounts must require a quorum of at least 3 signers for Critical Actions. **It must not be possible for quorum to be met with signers from a single entity** (no single entity will have enough signers to meet the quorum alone, and each critical action will therefore require approval from signers from at least 2 independent entities)."

A plain 3-of-N threshold protects against individual key loss and individual malice. It does not protect against an *organization* — one firm holding three signer slots can act alone, and a compromise of that firm's infrastructure, a coordinated internal fraud, or a court order directed at it captures the account outright. The independence condition converts the threshold from a count of keys into a count of organizations, so an attacker must breach two separate legal entities with separate infrastructure and separate incentives.

The eligible signer sets are small and named: Spark Asset Foundation "including legal council," Phoenix Labs, and the Spark Operational Facilitator (Arkis) or Spark Operational Executor Agent (offchain). Including legal counsel as an eligible signer is a deliberate diversification of *type* as well as entity — a lawyer's incentives, employer and threat surface differ from an engineer's, so collusion requires crossing a professional boundary too.

The residual weakness is that these entities are not fully independent in the economic sense. Phoenix Labs is a Nested Contributor to Spark; the Facilitator serves Spark; the Foundation funds both. Independence here is organizational and operational rather than adversarial — enough to defeat a single compromise, not enough to defeat a captured Spark.
description: Critical Actions need three signers with the explicit condition that no single entity can meet quorum alone, so compromising one organization is structurally insufficient.
